messages:
Incident Bot: ALERT: Elevated error rate + increased tail latency for embeddings in eu-central-1 detected ~08:47 UTC. Auto-paging to oncall (incident id: inc-2026-221).

Marta P: I'm on comms. @Tyler can you whip up a short initial statuspage blurb (initial + one interim + resolved)? Need legal quick-check before we go public.

Tyler W: Draft incoming. Keeping it concise for status subscribers.

Tyler W: ```
[Identified] 08:47 UTC: Partial degradation of embeddings in eu-central-1
Impact: Some customers in the EU may experience failed embeddings requests (5xx) or higher latency. Throughput for some workloads may be reduced. No evidence of data exposure.
Scope: Regional, affecting a subset of tenants.
Mitigation: Traffic steering to standby capacity and a lighter quantized model; autoscaling in progress. Engineering investigating root cause.
Status: Mitigating — next update in 30 minutes. Team aiming for recovery within ~60 minutes.
Guidance: Retry with exponential backoff. Open a support ticket for urgent production impact.
```

CS Ops: Can we add a line asking internal CS reps to identify any high-RPS customers so we can notify them directly? Also request top-10 list.

Marta P: Yes — add: "CS: identify high-RPS customers for targeted outreach." CS Ops please DM me the list.

Legal: Quick note — do not commit to a precise recovery window. Suggest: "Team is aiming for recovery within approximately 1 hour; we will provide updates every 30 minutes." Also avoid SLA wording.

Tyler W: Updated per legal:

Tyler W: ```
[Identified] 08:47 UTC: Partial degradation of embeddings in eu-central-1
Impact: Some embeddings requests in the EU may return 5xx or see increased latency. A subset of customers may experience reduced throughput. There is no indication of customer data loss or exposure.
Scope: Regional and partial — not all tenants affected.
Mitigation: We are steering traffic to standby capacity and a quantized model variant and have autoscaling enabled. Engineering is validating recovery steps.
Status: Mitigating — next public update in ~30 minutes. Team is aiming for recovery within approximately 1 hour.
Advice: If you encounter errors, please retry with backoff. Contact Support for high-priority concerns.
```

SRE Lead: For internal accuracy add this internal-only note before publish: "INTERNAL: shifted traffic to us-west fallback pool, warmed prefix KV cache, and rolled back a recent runtime kernel patch suspected in perf regression." Keep that out of public copy.

Eli: Ops update: shifted traffic to us-west pool at 08:56 UTC; observed immediate drop in 5xxs. We saw cache cold-start spikes during warmup — running controlled warmup batches now. Drained two hosts with CPU anomalies and replaced them. No OOMs.

Marta P: CS Ops — did you send the top-10 list?

CS Ops: Sent list to Marta via DM. Preparing targeted emails for top-5 with RPS notes and mitigation steps.

Tyler W: Ready to publish initial paragraph on status page. Requesting legal thumbs-up.

Legal: Looks fine 👍. Avoid saying "fix" — prefer "mitigated"/"recovered" wording later.

Marta P: Publishing initial update to status page and notifying subscribers. Posting link to #customer-facing-updates.

Incident Bot: STATUSPAGE_PUBLISHED: Initial public update posted at https://status.redwood.ai/incident/inc-2026-221 (08:59 UTC). Subscribers notified.

Eli: Follow-up ops note: prefix cache warmup reduced tail latency around 09:12 UTC. Most routed traffic shows baseline error rates by ~09:20 UTC. A very small set still see intermittent errors while cache continues to warm.

SRE Lead: We rolled back the kernel patch and paused recent runtime deployments pending a full perf signoff.

Marta P: Drafting ~30min public update — will state partial recovery and continue to avoid internal technical details.

Tyler W: 30-min update draft:

Tyler W: ```
[Update] 09:17 UTC: Partial recovery for embeddings in eu-central-1
Impact: Error rates and latency have improved for many customers after traffic steering and cache warmup. A small subset may still encounter intermittent failures.
Mitigation: Continued routing to fallback capacity, prefix KV cache warmup underway, and autoscaling. Engineering monitoring closely.
Status: Mitigating — next update in 30 minutes.
```

CS Ops: Sending targeted notices to top-5 customers now with suggested retry/backoff guidance and assurance we prioritized their traffic.

Marta P: Publish 09:17 update. Also send a quick internal thread in #eng-oncall with the internal-only ops snippet.

Incident Bot: STATUSPAGE_UPDATED: Public update posted at 09:17 UTC.

(approx 40 minutes later)

Eli: Ops final: primary capacity recovered, routed pool stable. After draining bad hosts and rollback, no residual 5xxs observed on primary. Continuing to monitor for 1 hour.

Tyler W: Resolved draft:

Tyler W: ```
[Resolved] 09:55 UTC: Embeddings service restored for eu-central-1
Impact: The elevated error rates and latency have been mitigated. Customers should see normal performance; if you continue to experience issues, please open a support ticket.
Root cause: A runtime kernel change interacted poorly with cold KV cache warming under higher admission, causing elevated tail latency and errors.
Remediation: Kernel patch rolled back, prefix cache warmup executed, suspect hosts replaced, and autoscaling stabilized. An RCA will be published to affected customers and internally.
```

Legal: OK to publish resolved and include notice that an RCA will follow.

Marta P: Publishing resolved notice and sending closure emails to top customers with RCA timeline.

Incident Bot: STATUSPAGE_RESOLVED: Incident inc-2026-221 marked resolved at 09:55 UTC. Subscriber notifications sent.

Marta P: Thanks all — good cross-team coordination. I'll collate the bridge transcript and hand off the post-incident RCA to eng-ml/infra.

SRE Lead: RCA owner assigned to eng-ml/infra; draft ETA 48 hours.

Incident Bot: INCIDENT_CLOSED: Oncall handback complete.
